features.description: Rewrite the curriculum grounding preamble so the tutor stops opening every reply with 'According to <domain>'. Cite by TITLE, mid-sentence, only when the retrieved content carries the answer. Attribution is kept (Axiom 2); the ritual is dropped.
acceptance_criteria: No tutor reply opens with 'According to <domain>' or 'From <domain>'
The line-118 twin ('Always cite the source in your answer') is rewritten too, not just the line-53 preamble
_build_source_preamble emits the human title first with the domain parenthesised; filename fallback unchanged when no title exists
A load-bearing retrieved claim is still attributed, by title, in natural position
Asking 'where did that come from?' still yields a specific source
backend make test-fast stays green
features.notes: SCOPE CORRECTION found during TDD. The design doc said the preamble should emit the human title with the domain parenthesised - but MaterialRef had NO title field. It cached only `origin`, which CurriculumDoc documents as PROVENANCE ('uvm.dk', 'Haka Fysik', a teacher name). That is the actual root cause of Aswin's complaint: a title was never available for the tutor to cite, so a domain was the only thing it could name. Added MaterialRef.title (optional, defaults '') cached at citation time alongside origin, and wired ALL FOUR attach paths: MaterialsSection cite + upload-then-cite, applyCopilotProposal, and the backend attach_material proposal. Wiring the write paths was the point - `subject` (1.1.58) and `language` (1.1.63 M2) both shipped as model fields no write path set. Three guard tests assert the title reaches the MaterialRef and the save payload. Backend 2715 passed (+9), frontend 1526 passed (+3). Grew ~80 LOC over the 0.25d estimate; still inside the day.

features.description: Tell the tutor what workbench elements exist BEFORE the student touches them (registry-driven manifest block), and make ActivityConfig.language actually drive the tutor's language. Both edit compose_teacher_focus and both care about block ordering, so they are ONE milestone.
acceptance_criteria: With a table + chart + checklist authored and ZERO student interaction, the tutor's opening turn names the table

Manifest hard-capped at 2000 chars with item-wise truncation and a '(+N more)' suffix
Composed focus stays under the 10k SkillConfig instruction cap with a MAXIMAL config (50 checklist items + 5 tables + sim tutorBlock + solution + concept map) - write this test FIRST

An English activity still grounds correctly in Danish curriculum material (reading != speaking)
The teacher_focus.py:176 'Match the student's language' heuristic is narrowed to apply only when cfg.language is unset, or removed
Chart describer names the axes (uses 1.1.64's optional fields; harmless before M5)
inject_teacher_focus log line carries per-kind element counts

features.notes: The cap test (written first, per the plan) FOUND A PRE-EXISTING BUG. A maximal activity composed 10,962 chars against a 10,000-char SkillConfig.instructions cap - and the element manifest was only 2,000 of that. Two blocks were already unbounded before this milestone: the concept-map block (30 nodes = ~3,512 chars) and the solution task (2,000). Stacked with a 2,000-char teaching goal it was already over the cap BEFORE the manifest existed. It had never fired because nobody had authored a maximal activity, and when it did it would have failed at SEED time (platform_seed re-read after partial write), not at request time. Bounded all three: _CONCEPT_MAP_CAP=1500 (node-wise, keeps the run_checkpoint contract), _SOLUTION_TASK_CAP=500, manifest 2000, plus a _TOTAL_FOCUS_CAP=8000 belt-and-braces that logs loudly. Two regression tests pin it. DESIGN CHANGE vs the doc: the language directive is emitted only when the activity language differs from the 'da' default. Language is Literal['da','en'] defaulting to 'da', so it is never unset - emitting unconditionally would have rewritten every existing activity's prompt 8 days before the pilot, and broken two existing tests that assert focus == goal exactly. Residual gap accepted and documented: a Danish activity whose student writes English still gets an English tutor by inference. Post-pilot fix. Also removed 'Match the student's language' from SOLUTION_FEEDBACK_PROMPT - it conflicted with the explicit setting. CLI needed a backend endpoint: GET /api/activity-configs/resolved-focus/{class}/{activity}, owner-scoped, returns manifest + resolvedFocus + focusChars + elementCounts. Backend 2743 passed (+28). Frontend 1526 unchanged. Lint clean.

features.description: The ILO half. Give the tutor tools to tick teacher-authored checklist items from conversation, with mandatory evidence and a visible 'shared with the AI' trust card. Aswin's 'automatic ILO check' becomes a real feature rather than a missing one.
acceptance_criteria: list_checklist and mark_checklist_item registered only when cfg.checklist is non-empty
A checklist item ticks from conversation with a visible HumanToolUseCard showing the evidence
mark_checklist_item REJECTS a tick with an empty evidence_summary at the tool boundary
Tick state is per-GROUP (reuses the concept_progress store shape, not a third store) and survives reload and a new session id
Group is keyed off the VERIFIED JWT claim, never a tool argument - one group cannot tick another group's checklist
Never reads User.email (empty string for anonymous-group students)
ProgressChecklist visually distinguishes AI-ticked from student-ticked; the student can untick an AI tick
make audit-trust-cards passes
features.notes: SCOPE CHANGE approved by M mid-milestone, twice. (1) 'The AI helps auto-grade' - ProgressChecklist carried the OPPOSITE written principle ('student-driven, not auto-graded; the agent does NOT decide what's done'). M superseded it following Aswin's ask; the docstring and the student-facing footer text were rewritten rather than left contradicting the code. The student override survives and is the thing that keeps it honest: every AI mark carries one sentence of evidence, renders as a ChecklistMarkCard in chat, and tapping the step flips provenance to 'student'. (2) ONE STORE. Student ticks lived in sessionStorage keyed by skill - per BROWSER - which was already wrong under 1.1.53 (primary classroom shape = one group across separate devices): three group members had three private checklists that died with the tab. Adding AI ticks in group scope alongside would have made the split visible and worse. Both now round-trip checklist_progress/{group}:{activity}. sessionStorage remains ONLY as the builder-preview fallback (no group to record against). Est 380 LOC -> actual ~1120 because of this. Group id is captured in the tool closure from the VERIFIED JWT claim; a test asserts group_id is not in the tool signature at all. Teacher preview gets no tools and 403 on write rather than inventing a group. Gotcha: the API test 401'd on every case because auth.get_current_user is a DIFFERENT object from auth.firebase_auth.get_current_user - override the one the route imports. Backend 2772 passed (+27). Frontend 1541 passed (+15). Lint clean, audit-trust-cards green.

features.description: State the teacher's checklist as the activity's objectives and the curriculum as reference material for reaching them, ordered before the curriculum sources preamble. Directly answers 'the chat forces students to achieve goals from the curriculum only, not with my ILOs'.
acceptance_criteria: The ILO precedence block is emitted BEFORE the curriculum sources preamble in the composed instruction
Test asserts the relative order of the two blocks
A teacher-authored ILO is preferred over a conflicting curriculum objective
The curriculum preamble is not weakened - grounding still works
features.notes: THE DESIGN DOC HAD THE FIX BACKWARDS. It said 'emit the ILO block BEFORE the curriculum sources preamble'. Reading the real composition: the instruction is SKILL.md body (with {teacher_focus} substituted INSIDE it) + curriculum preamble appended after + image/style/opening/reactive. So the teacher's goals were ALREADY before the curriculum preamble - and this codebase's convention is 'later instruction wins' (stated explicitly on inject_interaction_style_preamble, which appends precisely so it can override the SKILL.md Socratic rule). First is the WEAK position. The curriculum preamble held the last word, which IS the mechanism behind Aswin's complaint, and doing what the doc said would have been a no-op. Fixed by stating precedence EXPLICITLY in the late position: build_ilo_precedence_block() is appended AFTER the curriculum preamble in agent.py and says the outcomes are the objectives while curriculum is reference for reaching them. Grounding is deliberately not weakened - a test asserts the block contains no 'ignore'/'do not use'. Bounded at 1200 chars like every other variable-length contributor. test_ilo_precedence_lands_AFTER_the_curriculum_preamble pins the order; if it inverts, the curriculum regains the last word and the complaint returns. Also surfaced iloPrecedence on GET /resolved-focus + `aiplatform activity manifest --full` - a prompt layer the debug command cannot render is the exact gap that hid the element blindness for six weeks. Backend 2778 passed (+6). Lint clean.
